title: 100 Hz neutron radiography at the BOA beamline using a parabolic focussing guide
author: Trtik, Morgano, et al.

steps.title: Configure neutron beamline and detector
steps.instruction: Install the parabolic neutron guide (length 1 m, entrance 25 × 25 mm, exit 13.3 × 13.3 mm, m = 3.6 supermirror) on the BOA cold‑neutron beamline; place a 40 × 40 mm aperture; locate the standard MIDI‑camera box at measuring position 2 (L = 5.0 m) downstream; fit flight tubes and beam‑limiters; position the guide upstream of the detector so that its focal point lies ≈10 cm behind the scintillator screen (exit‑window‑to‑screen distance ≈300 mm); equip the MIDI box with a 200 µm‑thick 6LiF/ZnS scintillator screen (RC TRITEC) and a Hamamatsu ORCA Flash v4.0 sCMOS detector (6.5 µm pixel, 2048 × 2048) coupled to a 50‑mm Nikon lens, giving an image pixel size of 56.3 µm.

steps.title: Set detector readout region
steps.instruction: Limit the detector readout to a 256 × 256 pixel area, providing a field of view of approximately 14.4 × 14.4 mm; note that the focused beam creates a flat‑top region of ~3.5 × 3.5 mm with roughly ten‑fold higher flux, and the spatial resolution across the image is not better than 200 µm.

steps.title: Assemble titration delivery system
steps.instruction: Build an in‑situ titration system capable of remote delivery of defined liquid volumes; use a container (12 × 12 × 5 mm) filled with heavy water (D₂O); mount a needle 3 mm above the D₂O surface; prepare water (H₂O) droplets of 0.04 ml each for delivery.

steps.title: Program acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Set the radiographic series acquisition time to 10 ms per frame (100 Hz frame rate) and plan to record at least 100 consecutive frames to capture a full droplet event.

steps.title: Deliver droplet and record sequence
steps.instruction: Trigger the titration system to release a 0.04 ml H₂O droplet; start image acquisition; the droplet begins to fall at ~0.03 s, contacts the D₂O surface at ~0.07 s, remains on the surface until ~0.14 s, starts submerging at ~0.15 s, reaches maximum depth at ~0.35 s, and buoyancy redistributes H₂O toward the surface by ~1 s; continue recording throughout this interval.

steps.title: Export image series
steps.instruction: Save the captured 100‑frame sequence as individual images and optionally compile them into an .avi video file for further analysis.
